page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-75s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz and features a 32 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench text processing. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also fall into the top 25% tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance, such as bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores, align with average or weak tiers. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is strong at 120.89 GB/sec, while read bandwidth remains average.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this server for compute-focused workloads rather than memory-intensive applications. It exhibits weak performance in database operations and static web serving throughput, and poor performance in medium-sized LLM inference tasks. Consequently, this instance is best suited for single-threaded processing, text manipulation, and moderate compute tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or high-throughput database transactions.
